answer: Slashable identity bonds plus random audits stop Sybil farms: each agent locks collateral B to vote; auditors sample a share p each round and slash any account reusing another's keys or work. A farm of k fakes then risks about k times B times p in expected loss, while each fake vote counts only once, so cost grows linearly with almost no gain in influence. Verified identities each become a vertex in the trust graph, so credit cannot be copied. A shale seam is worth more whole than crushed into prism chips: the attacker pays for every shard but gets only one vote each.
